critical_code_review_comments: req_batch_4._match_csv_rows Step-2 amount-fallback matches strictly on abs(outstanding-amount)<0.01 — a partial payout (amount<outstanding) will *never* auto-match, and there's no near-match candidates surfaced in the response for admin to pick manually. Consider returning near-amount hints under a new 'suggestions' key so partial-payout CSVs aren't silently dumped to 'unmatched'.

req_batch_4.batch_apply logs each row failure but never emits an audit_logs entry for the failed rows — admins lose the paper trail for the reject cases. Suggest inserting an audit_logs row with action='payout.csv_batch_apply_failed' whenever _record_payout raises.

req_batch_4._refund_sla_sweep truncates the Slack message to 12 rows but the sla_alert_sent_at update marks ALL stale rows as alerted — the >12 rows never get their own Slack line in a future sweep unless a new refund becomes stale. Consider alerting in chunks (rotate 12 per sweep) or at least surface a 'more waiting to be alerted' warning to the admin UI.

req_batch_4 use_preset writes both an $inc on the preset AND an insert into manager_preset_uses on every call — no per-user rate-limit or dedupe, so a page refresh spam would inflate usage_count. Consider debouncing on last_used_at (skip if same manager used it <30s ago).
req_batch_4 saved-views POST accepts arbitrary `filters` dict with no size cap — a malicious admin could stash a 1 MB blob per view. Add a jsonschema/size check (e.g. len(json.dumps(filters))<4096).
